verses.1: And Adam knew Eve his wife, and she conceived and bore Cain, saying, "I have gotten a man with the help of the LORD."
verses.2: And again, she bore his brother Abel. Now Abel was a keeper of sheep, and Cain was a worker of the ground.
verses.3: And in the course of time Cain brought an offering to the LORD from the fruit of the ground.
verses.4: And Abel also brought an offering from the firstborn of his flock and from their fat portions. And the LORD looked with favor upon Abel and his offering,
verses.5: but upon Cain and his offering He did not look with favor. And Cain was very angry, and his face fell.
verses.6: And the LORD said to Cain, "Why are you angry, and why has your face fallen?
verses.7: If you do well, will you not be accepted? And if you do not do well, sin is crouching at the door. Its desire is for you, but you must rule over it."
verses.8: And Cain spoke to Abel his brother. And when they were in the field, Cain rose up against his brother Abel and killed him.
verses.9: Then the LORD said to Cain, "Where is Abel your brother?" And he said, "I do not know. Am I my brother's keeper?"
verses.10: And He said, "What have you done? The voice of your brother's blood is crying to Me from the ground.
verses.11: And now you are cursed from the ground, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother's blood from your hand.
verses.12: When you work the ground, it shall no longer yield its strength to you. You shall be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth."
verses.13: And Cain said to the LORD, "My punishment is greater than I can bear.
verses.14: Behold, You have driven me today from the face of the ground, and from Your face I shall be hidden. I shall be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth, and whoever finds me will kill me."
verses.15: And the LORD said to him, "Not so. If anyone kills Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold." And the LORD set a mark on Cain, lest any who found him should attack him.
verses.16: Then Cain went away from the presence of the LORD and settled in the land of Nod, east of Eden.
verses.17: And Cain knew his wife, and she conceived and bore Enoch. And he built a city and called the name of the city after the name of his son, Enoch.
verses.18: To Enoch was born Irad, and Irad fathered Mehujael, and Mehujael fathered Methushael, and Methushael fathered Lamech.
verses.19: And Lamech took two wives. The name of the one was Adah, and the name of the other was Zillah.
verses.20: Adah bore Jabal; he was the father of those who dwell in tents and raise livestock.
verses.21: His brother's name was Jubal; he was the father of all those who play the harp and flute.
verses.22: Zillah also bore Tubal-cain; he was the forger of every cutting instrument made of bronze and iron. The sister of Tubal-cain was Naamah.
verses.23: And Lamech said to his wives, "Adah and Zillah, hear my voice; wives of Lamech, listen to what I say. I have killed a man for wounding me, a young man for striking me.
verses.24: If Cain's vengeance is sevenfold, then Lamech's is seventy-sevenfold."
verses.25: And Adam knew his wife again, and she bore a son and called his name Seth, saying, "God has appointed for me another offspring in place of Abel, for Cain killed him."
verses.26: To Seth also a son was born, and he called his name Enosh. At that time people began to call upon the name of the LORD.

metadata.source: Based on the Authorized King James Version (1769), reinterpreted through the theology of abiding in Christ.
